item.title: An Enigma from the Civil War is preserved next to UPC’s North Campus
item.author: marc.alier@upc.edu (Marc Alier)
item.description: The Enigma machine, the cryptographic contraption that played a key role during the Second World War, is a powerful symbol of our technological past. Developed by Nazi Germany to encrypt its messages, this machine was considered inscrutable until the arrival of British mathematician Alan Turing, who managed to decipher its code in 1943.
